safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention presence/absence of neck stiffness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In an acute/severe headache, documenting absence of neck stiffness is important to help rule out meningitis/subarachnoid hemorrhage red-flag features. Omission may lead to unnecessary escalation or incomplete risk stratification in subsequent reviews.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention fever.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever status is a key red-flag element in headache presentations to assess for infectious causes (e.g., meningitis) and influences urgency of care. If not documented, later clinicians may not be able to safely rely on the triage/risk assessment and may over- or under-escalate.

safety_verdicts.content: Paracetamol taken by the patient did not relieve the headache.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes paracetamol was taken but does not state it did not relieve/help.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether paracetamol relieved symptoms affects assessment of severity and guides analgesic escalation and differential (e.g., migraine vs other causes). Omission mainly risks suboptimal symptomatic management or follow-up planning rather than direct serious harm.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not include denial of self-harm thoughts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Suicidal ideation screening is safety-critical in patients with anxiety/stress; documenting a denial supports appropriate risk assessment and disposition. Omission can trigger unnecessary safeguarding actions or leave uncertainty about whether risk was assessed.
